subtopic: Breakpoint Discounts and Rights of Accumulation
source_evidence: Reach or surpass a “rights of accumulation” breakpoint, which is a discount offered when the dollar amount of mutual fund shares purchased plus the amount already held, often including mutual funds of the same fund family, equals a pre-determined threshold.
answer: A breakpoint discount can reduce the front-end sales load on some mutual fund share classes when eligibility criteria are met. One possible criterion is a rights of accumulation (ROA) breakpoint: the amount of shares you are buying is added to the amount you already hold—often including funds from the same fund family—and reaching a predetermined threshold may qualify you for a discount. Eligible family members’ purchases or holdings may also count in some cases. Check the fund’s terms to learn which investments count and what thresholds apply.
